title: A Shared Linear-Referencing Framework for Comparing Authoritative and Open Road-Network Data and Navigation Restrictions
content: High-quality, consistent digital road networks and navigation restrictions are fundamental to geospatial analysis and transport applications. Governments maintain authoritative road databases, while open initiatives such as Overture Maps (OM) provide data with global coverage. Despite overlapping scopes, systematic, reproducible approaches for establishing a shared analytical basis across such heterogeneous road-network datasets remain limited. This paper presents a shared linear-referencing framework that uses cross-network correspondences to derive common analytical units for systematic comparison of road-network properties, quality assessment, and information transfer across heterogeneous road-network representations. The framework was evaluated and subsequently applied using data from the authoritative Norwegian Road Database (NVDB) and OM across areas with differing spatial characteristics. The evaluation demonstrated 98.9% correspondence coverage across urban and rural environments, while 98.5% of correspondences in a stratified manual validation sample were assessed as correct. Systematic differences were identified in network representation and in the completeness and values of navigation-related properties. Speed limits were identical for 67% of the compared network length, diverged for 6.5%, and 26.5% lacked this information in OM. The datasets showed substantial discrepancies in speed limits and traffic-flow directions, with errors in both. The discrepancies were not uniformly distributed; they followed systematic patterns associated with specific road classes, speed-limit categories, and urban road environments. The results highlight the complementary strengths and limitations of authoritative and open road-network datasets and demonstrate the value of systematic comparison for quality assessment and information transfer. They further highlight the importance of systematic quality assessment to maintain trust in authoritative datasets.
